items.title: Bersatu will be given chance to defend itself before PN takes action — Rafique
items.summary: MELAKA: Bersatu leaders should remain patient and refrain from making assumptions about possible disciplinary action by Perikatan Nasional (PN) against the party after the Melaka election. He said, as stated by PN chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar, the coalition was gathering evidence related to allegations of misconduct before taking further action. "Yesterday, Datuk Seri Samsuri made it clear that PN would take disciplinary action, but evidence must first be gathered because we do not want to punish anyone without proof.

items.title: Melaka polls: BN, PN target 60 per cent voter support
items.summary: Umno Supreme Council member Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Maslan said the target was based on the percentage of votes secured by BN and PN respectively in the 15th General Election (GE15), at 29 per cent and 31 per cent. "In GE15, BN secured 29 per cent of the votes, PN 31 per cent, while Pakatan Harapan obtained 38 per cent. "When BN and PN work together, we can combine the support, with 29 plus 31 equalling 60 per cent.

items.title: Netanyahu again seeks unity government despite mandate denial
items.summary: JERUSALEM: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu called again Monday for a unity government that would keep him in power, a day after opposition rival Gadi Eisenkot was given a mandate to form a coalition. "A unity government is, simply, a necessity," Netanyahu said in a video posted on social media that ignored President Isaac Herzog on Sunday formally giving Eisenkot the first chance at a government. Netanyahu's bloc won 53 seats.

items.title: Eight missing, nine stranded in Sungai Pertak water surge
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Eight people remain missing after being swept away by strong currents, while nine others are stranded in three separate incidents following a water surge at Sungai Pertak in Kuala Kubu Baru this evening. The incidents involved three separate groups. Selangor Fire and Rescue Department assistant operations director Ashrul Riezal Asbar said the eight missing comprised one member of a group of Yemeni and locals, and seven members of a group of 11 locals.

items.title: Umno will not let past disputes derail cooperation with Pas
items.summary: MELAKA: Umno has no intention of revisiting past disagreements with Pas, choosing instead to focus on political cooperation and the people's well-being, Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki said. The Umno secretary-general said past differences and contentious issues should no longer stand in the way of efforts to build mutual understanding and strengthen the spirit of cooperation between the parties. He said both parties had agreed to put the past behind them and focus on a bigger agenda, particularly the interests of the people and the future of the state and country.

items.title: PN members told to vote for BN candidates
items.summary: TANGGA BATU: All Perikatan Nasional members have been instructed to vote for Barisan Nasional candidates in the Melaka election on Nov 14. PN secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan said the directive was aimed at ensuring a strong victory for the two coalitions in the state election. "This is nothing new for PN.

items.title: Trump casts doubt on US midterm results with new fraud claims
items.summary: WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump renewed baseless allegations of voter fraud on Monday, questioning the legitimacy of last week's midterm elections after Democrats swept both chambers of Congress in a crushing defeat for his Republican Party. "Does anybody really believe that this 'Election' was honest. Trump wrote on Truth Social, alleging without evidence that large early-voting "dumps" had made Republican victories impossible.

items.title: Kedah MB's 1979 speech on wartime refuge transcribed after 47 years
items.summary: The speech was delivered on Dec 14, 1979, at the commemorative stone-laying ceremony for Kampung Lindungan Raja in Sedim, Kulim. It recounts historical events in Sedim during the Japanese occupation, including how the late Sultan Abdul Hamid was given refuge in the village. "The audio recording is still kept by the Malaysian Historical Society Kedah branch.

items.title: Cruise ship pianist rescued after 9 hours at sea
items.summary: LOS ANGELES: A pianist working on a cruise ship was rescued by two fishermen after drifting for nine hours in the Pacific Ocean about 30km off the coast of California, US media reported. The circumstances under which the 37-year-old man fell overboard from the Ovation of the Seas, a Royal Caribbean ship bound for Mexico, are unknown, CBS News reported. In the incident, which occurred on Friday, two fishermen — Grant Garrett and Sean Norton — were returning from marlin fishing near Santa Catalina Island, part of Los Angeles County, when they spotted the man in the open sea.

items.title: Wealth of the nation belongs to the people, not politicians
items.summary: MELAKA: The country's wealth should be used to improve the people's welfare, rather than to make elected representatives and political leaders wealthy, said Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail. The Pakatan Harapan secretary-general, who is also home minister, said the primary responsibility of elected representatives was to resolve the people's problems, not use their positions to amass wealth. Oil prices are rising.

items.title: What the US midterms mean for Malaysia and the region
items.summary: THE midterms have shifted the balance of power in Washington, but whether they will alter American foreign policy is an open question. At first blush, congressional control by the Democrats may constrain Trump at home but let us not forget he is still the president and one who wields significant veto powers. American policy is increasingly shaped by forces that do not always pull in the same direction.

items.title: NST Leader: No more temporary fixes — Malaysia needs a drainage overhaul
items.summary: This means the natural landscape and its capacity to absorb rainfall will inexorably give way to paved and concreted cityscapes, where only adequate drainage systems can spare us from inevitable floods during the rainy season or even the occasional heavy thunderstorm. Social activist Tan Sri Lee Lam Thye has a point when he says Malaysia must move beyond repeated drain-clearing exercises and adopt a long-term flood mitigation strategy. The country's ageing drainage infrastructure, as well as woefully inadequate drainage systems in most towns and cities, needs an overall review.

items.title: Google unveils new AI chip variants as cloud demand surges
items.summary: BENGALURU: Alphabet's Google introduced two new variations of its in-house tensor processing units (TPUs) on Monday, stepping up its challenge to Nvidia's dominance in the booming artificial intelligence chip market. Google's TPUs have primarily been used internally for products such as Search, YouTube and Gemini, but the company has been making the chips available through its cloud business to attract enterprise AI customers. The new chips, 8tx and 8i Max, are redesigned versions of existing processors tailored to specific customer needs, according to the company.

items.title: Melaka Pas confident cooperation with Umno will last beyond three years
items.summary: MELAKA: Melaka Pas has dismissed claims that its cooperation with Umno would not last beyond three years. Its commissioner, Zulkifli Ismail, said the remarks came from those opposed to the unity efforts between the two major parties under Muafakat Melaka, an understanding between Perikatan Nasional and Barisan Nasional. He said PN and BN were committed to sustaining the cooperation, which was intended to extend beyond electoral contests.

items.title: Single mother appeals for missing teenage daughter to return home
items.summary: Nurul Aida Alias, 34, said she was worried because her second child of six, Wan Zulaikha Mohd Zafari, had left home without taking any identification documents. Nurul Aida said she had lodged a police report and hoped her daughter would be found safe soon. "Please come home, dear.

items.title: Abu Dhabi talks must show if Russia 'genuinely prepared' to negotiate: German FM
items.summary: PARIS: US-mediated talks this week in Abu Dhabi between Russia and Ukraine on ending the war sparked by Russia's invasion will show whether Moscow is truly ready to negotiate a settlement, German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul said on Monday. [[nid:1574250]] Speaking after talks with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Wadephul said they "agreed that there is a chance to end Russia's war of aggression against Ukraine through negotiations". But he added: "The prerequisite is that Russia finally abandons its maximalist demands."

items.title: PN has strong evidence for action against Bersatu, says Takiyuddin
items.summary: MELAKA: Perikatan Nasional has strong evidence to justify its proposal to take disciplinary action against Bersatu, its secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan said. He said the proposed action also covered Bersatu's complaint to the Registrar of Societies (RoS), which resulted in PN's registration being cancelled before the matter was challenged in court. Takiyuddin said PN would proceed with disciplinary action against Bersatu after the Melaka election.

items.title: Saifuddin: Nana's energy, proactive approach can deliver for Klebang
items.summary: KLEBANG: Age is no barrier to delivering results when backed by a sharp mind and the energy needed in frontline politics, said Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail. Defending Pakatan Harapan's (PH) decision to field a young candidate in Klebang, the coalition's secretary-general said Farzana Hayani Mohd Nasir had the qualities needed to earn public trust and serve at grassroots level. Saifuddin said Farzana, fondly known as Nana, had the focus and intellectual ability to address community concerns.

items.title: Malaysia calls for connectivity beyond populated areas
items.summary: DOHA: Malaysia has called for a broader approach to global digital connectivity that goes beyond populated areas to include key economic locations as reliable internet access becomes increasingly vital to economic growth and resilience. Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said Malaysia was exploring the Coverage of Economic Areas (CoEA) concept to complement the existing Coverage of Populated Areas (CoPA) approach, reflecting the need to ensure digital infrastructure supports economic activities and national development. He said Malaysia had made significant progress in expanding its digital infrastructure through the National Digital Network Plan (Jendela), particularly in underserved areas.

items.title: Malaysia developing national plan for post-quantum cryptography – Fahmi
items.summary: DOHA: Malaysia is developing a national plan to transition critical information infrastructure to post-quantum cryptography. Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said he had instructed the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) to engage with the National Security Council (NSC), National Cyber Security Agency (Nacsa) and telecommunications operators to establish a shared research and development (R&D) testbed. "Malaysia is developing a national plan to move critical information infrastructure to post-quantum cryptography.

items.title: Three cousins killed by lightning had been inseparable since childhood
items.summary: Their uncle, Haris Salleh Kurais, 42, said the three had been inseparable since growing up in their hometown in Semporna, Sabah, before settling and working here. Then someone else said they had been struck by lightning. Haris said the three had always been close and respected him as their uncle.

items.title: China dismisses spying allegations linked to Nvidia CEO's affair
items.summary: BEIJING: China's Foreign Ministry has rejected allegations of Chinese espionage linked to Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang's affair, dismissing them as fabricated and defamatory. Ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun made the remarks on Monday, German news agency dpa reported. The chief executive of the US chipmaker recently admitted to having had an affair, prompting Nvidia to launch an investigation.

items.title: MoH prepares 85 medical teams, 387 personnel for monsoon floods
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The Health Ministry has prepared 85 emergency medical teams comprising 387 personnel to respond to possible flooding during the 2026/2027 northeast monsoon, with psychological support also being lined up for affected communities. The ministry said these comprised 36 Rapid Assessment and Health Rapid Response Teams, 34 Medical Rapid Response Teams and 15 Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS) teams, Bernama reported. Through the National Crisis Preparedness and Response Centre (CPRC), State Health Departments, District Health Offices and healthcare facilities nationwide, the ministry has also stepped up preparedness to ensure continued healthcare services, particularly in flood-prone areas.

items.title: Traffic slows on major highways as Deepavali holidaymakers return
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Traffic is moving slowly along several stretches of major highways tonight as holidaymakers begin their journey home following the end of the Deepavali break. A Malaysian Highway Authority (MHA) spokesman said that as of 8pm, northbound traffic on the North-South Expressway (Plus) E1 was slow from Bidor to Tapah, Kuala Kangsar to Changkat Jering, Bukit Merah to Bandar Baharu, Jawi to Bandar Cassia, and Juru to Perai. Meanwhile, on the Plus E2, northbound traffic was sluggish from Jasin to Ayer Keroh, Simpang Ampat to Senawang, Port Dickson to Seremban, Simpang Ampat to Pedas Linggi, Putra Mahkota to Bangi, and the Sungai Besi Toll Plaza towards the city centre.

items.title: 1,084 flood victims sheltering at relief centres in three states
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 1,084 flood victims were taking shelter at temporary relief centres in three states as of 8pm today. A check of the Welfare Department's InfoBencana portal found that the victims were housed at 12 relief centres in Selangor, Perak and Sarawak. Selangor recorded the highest number of evacuees, with 694 people from 190 families at seven relief centres across four districts — Kuala Selangor, Hulu Langat, Gombak and Sabak Bernam.

items.title: COP31: Malaysia proposes 20pc of urban climate funds go directly to communities
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia has proposed that at least 20 per cent of multilateral urban climate financing be channelled directly to local authorities and communities in informal settlements to strengthen their capacity to adapt to climate change. Housing and Local Government Minister Nga Kor Ming, who is leading Malaysia's delegation to the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31), proposed the establishment of a Direct-to-Community Urban Climate Facility to channel the funds through predictable block grants. Nga said Malaysia's integrated approach to housing and local government allowed national climate adaptation targets to be put into practice through building regulations, energy efficiency measures, and urban planning guidelines across its 156 local authorities.

items.title: News@9: Today's top headlines - November 9, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: Early voting Preparations are in full swing at early voting centres across the state ahead of tomorrow's early voting for the 16th Melaka election. K9 hero 'Lexi' dies After nearly a decade of dedicated service in search and rescue operations, ' Lexi ', a Fire and Rescue Department K9 unit sniffer dog, has died. Special aid Eligible flood victims in Selangor will receive RM2,500 each in special additional cash assistance , with payments expected to begin tomorrow.

items.title: Melaka polls: Paya Rumput Indian community wants better-paying jobs, temple assistance
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 9 — Competitively paid job opportunities and assistance for the upkeep of places of worship are among the key issues raised by the Indian community in the Paya Rumput state constituency, which they hope will receive attention from the candidates elected during the Melaka state election. Mechanical engineer Sathesh Kumaar A/L Gunasegaran, 24, said graduate employability and competitive salaries were important benchmarks in determining who should be elected to serve the residents of Paya Rumput. K Selvie a/p Kannon, 58, said the Indian community in the constituency appreciated federal government assistance such as the Rahmah Cash Contribution (STR), Rahmah Basic Contribution (SARA) and other forms of aid, but also hoped that the needs of places of worship would be addressed.

items.title: Melaka polls: Anwar appeals armed forces, police personnel to back PH
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Pakatan Harapan chairman Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has appealed to armed forces and police personnel voting early in the Melaka election tomorrow to place their trust in PH candidates. "Tomorrow, our friends and families from the armed forces and police will fulfil their responsibilities as early voters in Melaka. A total of 12,531 eligible early voters, comprising 9,769 military personnel and their spouses and 2,762 police personnel will cast their ballots across 31 gazetted early polling centres statewide tomorrow.

items.title: Melaka polls: Anwar urges military, police voters to back Pakatan candidates
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 9 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) chairman Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has called on members of the Malaysian Armed Forces (ATM), their spouses and Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) personnel involved in the early voting process in the 16th Melaka State Election tomorrow to place their trust in PH candidates. “Tomorrow, our friends and families from the ATM and PDRM will fulfil their responsibilities as early voters in Melaka. A total of 12,531 eligible early voters, comprising 9,769 military personnel and their spouses and 2,762 police personnel will cast their ballots across 31 gazetted early polling centres statewide tomorrow.

items.title: Pahang Sultan opens Malaysia Pavilion at COP31 in Turkiye
items.summary: KUANTAN: The Sultan of Pahang, Al-Sultan Abdullah Ri'ayatuddin Al-Mustafa Billah Shah, today officiated the opening of the Malaysia Pavilion at the 31st Conference of the Parties to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (COP31) in Antalya, Turkiye. Tengku Ampuan Pahang Tunku Azizah Aminah Maimunah Iskandariah was also in attendance. The COP31 conference gathers world leaders, government representatives, international organisations, and various stakeholders to strengthen global cooperation in tackling climate change and accelerate the implementation of existing climate action commitments.

items.title: Four students caught cheating using AI glasses at middle, high schools in South Korea
items.summary: SEOUL: Four cases of cheating using artificial intelligence (AI) glasses have been reported at middle and high schools this year, South Korea's Education Ministry said on Monday, Yonhap News Agency reported. According to data collected from all 5,679 middle and high schools nationwide between Oct 27 and last Tuesday, one middle school student and three high school students were caught using AI glasses during their midterm or final examinations. Three of the four students were caught repeatedly touching their glasses, while the other was caught switching to AI glasses after the examination had begun.

items.title: Kajang woman arrested over alleged vandalism of electrical panel with ‘Allah’ inscription, cross
items.summary: Kajang district police chief Assistant Commissioner Naazron Abdul Yusof said the woman was detained by a team from the district police headquarters' Criminal Investigation Division at about 2.15pm today, Kosmo! He said the arrest followed a police report lodged at 12.16pm yesterday over a video circulating on social media that allegedly showed the woman carrying out the act. “Following the report, police managed to arrest a local woman in her 40s to assist in investigations.

items.title: Health Ministry deploys 387 personnel in 85 teams for monsoon flood response
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Nov 9 — The Ministry of Health (MOH) has prepared 85 Emergency Medical Teams comprising 387 personnel to respond to possible flooding during the 2026/2027 North-east Monsoon (MTL). In a statement today, the ministry said these comprised 36 Rapid Assessment and Health Rapid Response Teams, 34 Medical Rapid Response Teams and 15 Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS) teams. Through the National Crisis Preparedness and Response Centre (CPRC), State Health Departments, District Health Offices and healthcare facilities nationwide, the ministry has also stepped up preparedness to ensure continued healthcare services, particularly in flood-prone areas.

items.title: Kelantan deploys almost 60 psychological support workers to help flood victims cope with trauma
items.summary: Kelantan Department of Social Welfare (JKM) director Che Samsuzuki Che Noh said that in addition to providing psychological support, the team will also organise various activities to help reduce the emotional stress of the victims while they are at the PPS. He said that the Kelantan JKM also mobilised 400 officers and staff, 13 counselling officers, and 327 volunteers to ensure the smooth operation of disaster management and aid distribution. He added that early registration also helps expedite the BWI payment process, including after the PPS is closed.

items.title: Melaka polls: 12,531 military, police personnel and spouses to cast early ballots tomorrow
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 9 — Some 12,531 eligible early voters in the 16th Melaka State Election will cast their ballots across 31 gazetted early polling centres statewide tomorrow. The election sees Pakatan Harapan fielding candidates in 24 state seats, followed by Barisan Nasional (23), Parti Bersama Malaysia (16), Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (seven), Perikatan Nasional (five), Parti Pribumi Perkasa Malaysia (one), and three Independents. In the 2021 Melaka State Election, Barisan Nasional won 21 seats to form the state government, while Pakatan Harapan won five seats and Perikatan Nasional two.

items.title: ECRL enters final trial run ahead of Dec 12 passenger service launch
items.summary: GOMBAK, Nov 9 — Malaysia Rail Link Sdn Bhd (MRL) is conducting trial operations for the East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) as part of the final preparations ahead of the planned launch of commercial passenger services on December 12, 2026. MRL said in a statement that the trial operations programme is intended to assess operational readiness, service efficiency, station management and the passenger experience under actual operating conditions, Kosmo! Running from November 7 to December 2, 2026, the programme covers journeys between Gombak and Kota Bharu in both directions, and includes express and transit services.

items.title: Lexi’s final mission: Sabah rescue dog dies after helping find missing man following nine years of service
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Nov 9 — A Sabah Fire and Rescue Department search dog died a day after completing its final search-and-rescue mission, bringing nearly nine years of service with the department’s K9 unit to an end. Lexi had taken part in a search operation for a missing person in Kampung Pulutan Membawang, Menggatal, on November 5, making it the dog’s final assignment with the rescue team. Sabah Fire and Rescue Department K9 unit chief Calvin Joe Jeafery said Lexi had been accompanied by its handler, fireman Arthur Anderson Walter, during the operation.

items.title: Three killed by lightning strike in Bandar Baru Salak Tinggi, police confirm
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 9 — Three people were killed after being struck by lightning in an incident in Bandar Baru Salak Tinggi in Sepang this afternoon. Sepang District Police Chief Assistant Commissioner Norhizam Bahaman confirmed the incident when contacted, Kosmo! “Yes,” he said briefly when contacted to confirm the incident.

items.title: Repeat drug-positive driver arrested after another crash in Kuala Pilah
items.summary: KUALA PILAH, Nov 9 — A male driver who was previously involved in an accident involving five vehicles and tested positive for drugs was again involved in an accident along Jalan Seremban-Kuala Pilah, near Tanjong Ipoh town, here, last Saturday. Kuala Pilah District Police Chief Supt Muhamad Mustafah Hussin said the accident at about 2.45pm was believed to have occurred when a Toyota Vios driven by the suspect, travelling from Seremban towards Bahau, rammed into the rear of a Nissan Grand Livina multi-purpose vehicle (MPV). The suspect was arrested and taken to the Kuala Pilah District Police Headquarters for further investigation,” he said in a statement today.

items.title: Paya Terubong landslide: Penang to decide developer’s fate after DOSH probe
items.summary: Penang Local Government and Town and Country Planning Committee chairman H’ng Mooi Lye said the state government would await the outcome of DOSH’s investigation before deciding on further action. “We will await DOSH’s findings,” he told Bernama when contacted to comment on possible action against the project developer. However, the developer must first submit Pre-Construction Information (PCI) documents to DOSH for assessment before mitigation works can begin.

items.title: Nacsa records 5,110 cyber incidents in Malaysia from January to September
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 9 — The National Cyber Security Agency (Nacsa) recorded 5,110 cybersecurity incidents from January to September this year, compared with 5,837 incidents last year. Nacsa chief executive Dr Megat Zuhairy Megat Tajuddin said the higher number of incidents recorded last year was largely driven by intrusion attempts and potential attacks, which were detected at an early stage. He said Nacsa’s National Cyber Coordination and Command Centre (NC4) had also issued nine alerts and advisories in October and November this year, concerning security vulnerabilities affecting National Critical Information Infrastructure (NCII) entities and government agencies.

items.title: Toddler goes missing during family outing at Gopeng river, search underway
items.summary: Perak Fire and Rescue Department Operations Division assistant director Sabarodzi Nor Ahmad said a team from the Gopeng Fire and Rescue Station was dispatched to the scene after receiving a call at 12.06pm. Personnel from the Kampar Fire and Rescue Station were also assisting by monitoring the river downstream near Kampar, he said, adding that the search is still ongoing. Sabarodzi said the Pangkor Fire and Rescue Station team was mobilised after receiving a call at 12.54pm.

items.title: Selangor flood evacuees more than double to 583 as Perak numbers ease
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 9 — The number of flood evacuees in Selangor more than doubled, while Perak recorded a slight improvement, bringing the total number of victims sheltering at six temporary relief centres in the two states to 1,002 as of this afternoon In Selangor, the number of evacuees rose to 583 people from 163 families as of 3.40pm, compared with 215 people from 55 families this morning. According to the Social Welfare Department’s (JKM) InfoBencana portal, all the evacuees were housed at four relief centres in Kuala Selangor, namely Sekolah Kebangsaan (SK) Dato’ Maharaja Lela, which accommodated 326 people from 97 families; SK Parit Mahang (154 people, 36 families); Sekolah Agama Batu 8 Ijok (77 people, 21 families); and SK Jaya Setia (26 people, nine families). In Perak, the number of victims in Hilir Perak declined slightly to 419 people from 124 families, compared with 439 people from 130 families this morning.

items.title: Broke Malaysian overstays in Batam, allegedly robs woman for cash, steals SUV and injures cop before arrest
items.summary: BATAM, Nov 9 — A 41-year-old Malaysian man has been arrested in Batam, Indonesia, after allegedly robbing a woman at gunpoint with an airsoft pistol, stealing her car and injuring a police officer while attempting to escape last Friday. The suspect, from Melaka, allegedly threatened the 48-year-old woman with an airsoft pistol and a knife before fleeing in her Toyota Rush with valuables worth an estimated 292 million rupiah (RM73,000), Sinar Harian reported today. Barelang Police Criminal Investigation Division chief Commissioner Tri Poerbowo said preliminary investigations found that the suspect had entered Indonesia on September 15 for a holiday but overstayed by 10 days after running out of money.

items.title: Anwar announces RM2,500 flood aid for each eligible household in Selangor
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 9 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today announced a special additional cash aid of RM2,500 for heads of eligible flood-affected households in Selangor, with payments expected to begin tomorrow. Meanwhile, speaking to reporters after visiting flood victims in Kuala Selangor, Anwar said the additional RM2,500 aid is intended for families who have endured prolonged displacement and sustained substantial damage from the disaster. The prime minister said the additional aid, placed under the Prime Minister’s Department’s Implementation Coordination Unit (ICU), is being provided in view of the protracted flood situation and the heavier losses incurred by victims.

items.title: ‘Our first priority was grandma’ — families share flood ordeal in Hilir Perak
items.summary: TELUK INTAN, Nov 9 — As floodwaters rose around their homes, two families in Hilir Perak faced an urgent challenge — getting their vulnerable loved ones to safety before the situation worsened. For Mahani Zakaria, 75, protecting her 41-year-old son with disabilities and two orphaned grandchildren mattered far more than saving her belongings when floodwaters began entering her home in Kampung Batu 10, Changkat Jong, several days ago. She and her family were evacuated to the temporary relief centre at the Teluk Intan Municipal Council (MPTI) Rest House Hall at about 2 am.

items.title: Three Malaysians arrested in Mauritius after 76kg cannabis seizure at airport
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 9 — Mauritian authorities arrested three Malaysians after seizing 76.14kg of suspected cannabis from their luggage at Sir Seewoosagur Ramgoolam International Airport. According to Free Malaysia Today (FMT), the suspects, comprising two men aged 30 and 22 and an 18-year-old woman, were detained after arriving in Mauritius on an Emirates flight from Dubai on November 2. The Mauritius Revenue Authority said the discovery was made after officials stopped the trio for questioning and inspected their checked baggage.

items.title: Return rush begins, major highways congested as Deepavali holiday wraps up
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 9 — Traffic flow on several major highways heading towards the Klang Valley was congested as of 3pm today, as city dwellers began returning home following the Deepavali holiday. A spokesperson for the Malaysian Highway Authority (LLM) said on the North-South Expressway (PLUS), slow-moving traffic was reported from Sungai Petani Selatan to Bertam, Sungai Dua to Juru Autocity, Kuala Kangsar to the Meru Tunnel, Simpang Pulai to Gopeng, and Gopeng to Bidor. “Meanwhile, for the southern route, congestion is occurring from Kulai to Simpang Renggam, Ayer Keroh to Simpang Ampat, Pedas Linggi to Port Dickson, Bandar Ainsdale to Nilai Utara, Southville City to Kajang, and from Sungai Besi towards the city centre,” the spokesperson told Bernama today.

items.title: Melaka polls: Pakatan pledges grants for women traders, proposes more childcare centres, says Adly Zahari
items.summary: Melaka PH chairman Adly Zahari said the grants were aimed at strengthening household incomes in the state. He said the grants, offered under the Women Empowerment aspiration in the ‘Melaka Rumah Kita’ manifesto, would also cater to the actual needs of traders, including purchasing equipment, increasing stock and expanding production capacity. Elaborating, Adly, who is also the PH candidate for the Bukit Katil seat, said PH wanted to help women running small businesses and small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) expand their businesses according to their respective needs.

items.title: Minister says Puspal, Jakim verifying claims of religious sensitivity breach at The Weeknd concert
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 9 — Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Senator Dr Zulkifli Hasan has said that firm action will be taken if The Weeknd’s concert in Bukit Jalil is found to have breached religious sensitivities. “All parties must ensure that artistic performances do not cause confusion related to faith, morals, and religious sensitivities in Malaysia,” he said. “Firm action based on law and verified facts will be taken to ensure every performance by local and foreign artists always preserves religious sensitivities, culture, and public order,” he said.

items.title: Woman jailed three months, fined RM5,000 for dumping baby with missing head, arm in Kuala Berang drain
items.summary: KUALA BERANG, Nov 9 — A restaurant worker was sentenced to three months’ jail and fined RM5,000 by the Magistrate’s Court here today after pleading guilty to concealing the birth of her child by dumping the infant’s body in a drain. Magistrate Nur Athirah Hashim also ordered the accused, Nur Ain Adilin Mohd Rofiza, 23, to serve an additional five months in jail if she failed to pay the fine. “The accused’s guilty plea has saved the court and prosecution time.

items.title: Melaka polls: Pakatan’s Adly Zahari urges civil servants to consider govt’s efforts in raising their pay
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 9 — The various initiatives and policies implemented by the federal government for civil servants should be taken into consideration by the 12,531 security personnel and their spouses who will be casting their early votes in the 16th Melaka state election tomorrow. Melaka Pakatan Harapan (PH) chairman Adly Zahari said these initiatives include a 15 per cent salary increase for civil servants through the implementation of the Public Service Remuneration System (SSPA), in addition to the government’s efforts to strengthen the national economy. Adly, who is also the PH candidate for the Bukit Katil state constituency, said beyond economic performance and Malaysia’s international standing, he hopes civil servants will also take into account the efforts to strengthen integrity, transparency, and national governance when casting their votes tomorrow.

items.title: Melaka polls: Mandarin fluency a bonus for Pakatan’s Farzana in reaching Kelebang Chinese voters
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 9 — The ability to speak Mandarin gives Pakatan Harapan (PH) candidate for the Kelebang state constituency Farzana Hayani Mohd Nasir an advantage in reaching Chinese voters, particularly the elderly. “Being able to speak Mandarin makes it easier for Farzana to introduce herself to the Chinese community, especially the elderly, while building closer ties with them. “I like seeing Malays who can speak Chinese.

items.title: Police say pistol-wielding man in viral Kuala Lumpur chase was conducting anti-drug operation
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 9 — The man seen holding what appeared to be a pistol while pursuing a car in a viral video along Jalan Sultan Salahuddin here is believed to be a police officer involved in a special anti-drug operation on Saturday. According to Berita Harian (BH), Dang Wangi district police chief Assistant Commissioner Ahmad Azwan Amin Nordin said the incident occurred at about 6.30pm when a team from the Dang Wangi District Police Headquarters Narcotics Criminal Investigation Division spotted a suspicious black Honda Accord. Police managed to track down the vehicle again at about 6.40pm at the Jalan Sultan Salahuddin intersection before giving chase.

items.title: Ab Rauf: Melaka flood efforts to continue until issue resolved, RM432m allocated for Sungai Baru Hilir project
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 9 — The Melaka state government will continue its efforts to address flooding issues throughout the state until the root causes are identified and resolved, said Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh. He said a phased approach tailored to specific areas will continue to be implemented, taking into account various factors, including inadequate drainage systems and natural phenomena. In a related development, Ab Rauf noted that the state government’s commitment to the welfare of the people is also reflected in the ‘Wakil Rakyat Untuk Rakyat’ (WRUR) programme, which is implemented across all 28 State Legislative Assembly constituencies in the state.

items.title: Sabah’s next big question: Expand KKIA, or build a brand-new airport?
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Nov 9 — Sabah’s long-term aviation needs require careful consideration of whether Kota Kinabalu International Airport (KKIA) should be expanded at its existing site or replaced by a new airport at another location. The two proposals were discussed by aviation experts during a public forum titled ‘The Future of Kota Kinabalu International Airport: Retain, Expand or Relocate? Airport, Airline and Civil Aviation Strategy Consultant Edward Clayton said several options could be considered to increase KKIA’s capacity, including constructing a second runway, adopting an alternative runway configuration or developing a separate relief airport.

items.title: Attorney General says ‘glaring error’ in Najib court document caused confusion
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 9 — Attorney General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar yesterday raised questions over the accuracy and scrutiny applied in preparing an official court document used as the basis for implementing Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s house arrest order. According to Berita Harian (BH), Mohd Dusuki said the issue should never have arisen had the parties involved exercised greater care in reviewing the document. He was commenting on alleged defects in the Kuala Lumpur High Court’s Order of Discharge document relating to the former prime minister’s sentence, which has drawn attention from legal practitioners.

items.title: Fire tears through 24-door Kanowit longhouse, but all residents escape unharmed
items.summary: KANOWIT, Nov 9 — A 24-door longhouse, Rumah Seliau at Sungai Tuah here, was badly damaged in a fire on Monday. The Sarawak Fire and Rescue Department (Bomba) operations centre said it received a call about the incident at 1.39am. “Sixteen firefighters from Kanowit and Sibu Jaya fire stations were deployed to the scene, about 46km away.

items.title: After viral umbrella videos, Seberang Jaya Hospital assesses damage from leaks
items.summary: BUTTERWORTH, Nov 9 — An assessment of the damage and the implementation of control measures are currently underway at Seberang Jaya Hospital (HSJ), following ceiling leaks caused by an extraordinary overflow of rainwater during heavy downpours and strong winds last Saturday. “The incident, which occurred between 5.45pm and 7pm on Saturday, affected several locations across both the old building (Block A) and the new building (Block B). However, the majority of areas experiencing rainwater overflow were located within the old block of HSJ.
